bib.title: Foundations of Large Language Models, Chapter 6: Reasoning

read.skipped: PDF ends mid-sentence in section 6.7 Summary (page 32 of PDF); no further chapter text or reference list exists in the file.

question: How do LLMs reason, and how can reasoning be improved by prompting, inference-time compute scaling (sampling, search, verification) and training (SFT, process supervision, RL, on-policy distillation)?
contributions: Frames reasoning as System 2 text generation that allocates inference compute to hard problems
Casts inference-time scaling as search: sampling, search strategies, verification
Unifies process supervision, reward shaping, advantage and on-policy distillation as dense step-level training signals
Reviews evaluation (outcome vs process, Pass@k, Cons@k) and open issues; discusses latent reasoning, memorization, whether LLMs truly reason

results.claim: A reasoning chain for the John/Mary age problem gives 14, where a base LLM keyword-matches and guesses 20.
results.setup: Word problem in 6.1.1; illustrative, no model run.

results.claim: Reward shaping with step differences telescopes to the final step score: R = v_np - v_0, and a PRM confidence that rises 0.4 to 0.9 gives r2 = +0.5, then falls to 0.1 for r3 = -0.8.
results.setup: Eq 6.20-6.21, PRM confidence per step, v0 = 0; illustrative.

results.claim: Grokking: a small Transformer on modular arithmetic hits 100% train accuracy early with near-zero test accuracy, then test accuracy spikes to 100% after prolonged training.
results.setup: Small Transformer on binary operations in abstract algebra such as modular addition; training continued far past overfitting.
results.quote: Suddenly, the test accuracy spikes to 100% in a very short time.

results.claim: Many LLMs support 128K-token contexts; some support hundreds of thousands to one million tokens (Claude 3.5, Gemini 1.5).
results.setup: Context lengths as of the chapter's writing; vendor claims.
results.quote: many LLMs now support context lengths of up to 128K tokens,

results.claim: Self-consistency picks the answer with the most votes among N sampled paths (Eq 6.6); Cons@k scores that majority answer against ground truth; Pass@k = 1/N sum(1 - C(Ns-Ci,k)/C(Ns,k)).
Search gains plateau: model capability ceiling, and path diversity drops as search effort rises.

RL compute vs reasoning performance follows an S-shaped curve; bigger base model/MoE and longer context raise the ceiling, while loss or advantage-normalisation changes mainly improve compute efficiency.
results.source: Khatri et al., 2025; Tan et al., 2026
results.setup: Large-scale RL scaling-law studies; no numbers given in chapter.

results.claim: A smaller model given extra inference compute can outperform a much larger model forced to answer immediately.
results.setup: Stated without numbers (Snell et al. 2024 cited nearby).

results.claim: Outcome reward models give false positives; a path with wrong logic but correct answer 3 for 2x+4=10 would score high.

practices: Use CoT prompting (few-shot or 'Let's think step by step') as the simplest way to elicit reasoning (6.2).
Sample N paths with temperature plus top-k or top-p, then select by verifier (Best-of-N) or majority vote (self-consistency) (6.3.2).
Trade diversity against quality: raise temperature or add a diversity term lambda*D to the search score, since higher temperature degrades per-path quality (6.3.2.3).
Prefer process reward models over outcome reward models to avoid right-answer-wrong-reason false positives; aggregate step scores by min or mean (6.3.4.1).
Build PRM labels by human annotation or Monte Carlo rollouts from each step toward a known final answer (6.3.4.1).
Use formal systems (code execution, equivalence checkers) as verifiers where tasks allow, feeding error messages back to the model (6.3.4.3).
Wrap the reasoning in <think>...</think> tags in SFT data so it can be hidden from users (6.4.1).
Use shaped step rewards r_t = v_t - v_{t-1} and future return, or advantages (TD error or GRPO group standardisation) to cut variance (6.4.2).
Use on-policy distillation at token level to teach recovery from student's own deviations, accepting teacher-in-the-loop cost (6.4.3).
Build synthetic reasoning data by sampling teacher paths and keeping verified-correct ones; vary numbers and constraints in seed problems (6.4.4.2).
Evaluate with both outcome accuracy (normalised answers) and, where affordable, process checks; report Pass@k and Cons@k; guard against contamination with fresh or private benchmarks (6.5).

terms.definition: System 1: a model directly outputs the final answer in a single pass. System 2: the model allocates extra inference compute to explicitly generate intermediate reasoning steps.
the ability to generate a coherent sequence of intermediate steps to reach the final answer
by allocating more computational power during generation, the model can think more deeply to solve harder problems
Sample N paths and choose argmax of a verifier score v(x,y) (Eq 6.5).
Marginalise reasoning paths by majority vote over extracted final answers (Eq 6.6).
Evaluates only the final answer of a reasoning path.
Assigns a correctness score to each step conditioned on input and previous steps (Eq 6.9).
Prompts an LLM to critique steps in natural language; a score is P('Correct' as first token) (Eq 6.13-6.14).
the reasoning steps written inside the <think> tags
With outcome-only feedback the model is left to guess which exact step caused the failure.

the student model learns from its own generated trajectories, rather than from trajectories sampled from the teacher model; teacher gives token-level distributions, loss is KL(student||teacher) (Eq 6.29)
Probability at least one of k independent samples is correct: 1/N sum(1 - C(Ns-Ci,k)/C(Ns,k)) (Eq 6.31).
Accuracy of the majority-vote answer over k sampled paths (Eq 6.33).
dummy tokens that give the model extra computation in hidden layers before answering
feeds the last-layer output vector back to the input layer as a continuous thought instead of a discrete token
model generates hidden thought tokens before predicting each next token and is rewarded when they help
test accuracy jumps long after training accuracy reaches 100%
